scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service charge incurred 34 days ago, which is slightly outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Todd Anderson and I'm 65. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello, Mr. Anderson. I understand how frustrating it can be to return from travel and find an unexpected charge. I would be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide your account number and the email address associated with your subscription?
Sure, my account number is 8849201 and the email is todd.anderson@email.com.
Thank you for that information. For security purposes, could you please confirm the last four digits of the payment method on file and your billing zip code?
The card ends in 4492 and my zip code is 90210.

Perfect, thank you for verifying those details, Mr. Anderson. I have located your account and the charge from 34 days ago. While our 'Service Cancellation and Refund Policy' (Section 4.2) typically limits refunds to a 30-day window, I can see that you did initiate the cancellation request correctly on the day you intended. Given that you were traveling and this is your first such request, I am authorized to make a one-time exception to our policy.
Oh, that would be wonderful. I really appreciate your help with this.

It is my pleasure. I have processed the refund for the full amount of $49.99 back to your card ending in 4492. You should see the credit appear in your account within 3 to 5 business days, depending on your bank's processing time. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?

resolution_summary: The agent verified the customer's account and transaction details, acknowledged the policy limit, and exercised a one-time exception to issue a full refund for the service charge.
